title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Here \hat\Pi_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, which is free profinite on two generators. It carries the automorphisms induced by the S_3-symmetries: ρ (order 3) and σ_∞ (the involution fixing ∞ and swapping 0 and 1). The loops satisfy l_1 = σ_∞(l_0) = ρ(l_0). The integer ν is tied to the multiplier μ = 2ν+1 (the cyclotomic character, so ν plays the role of Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2). An element f, defined via formula (6), is the analogue of Drinfeld's f_σ(x,y). The elements g and h measure the failure of the two 'lacets' relations, which correspond to the 3-cycle and 2-cycle relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. The auxiliary elements ξ and η are twisted cocycles: ξ for ρ, and η for σ_∞, i.e. η·σ_∞(η) = 1.

Step 1. Formula (28) from the previous page reads h = c·η^{-1}·σ_∞(c)^{-1} with c = f^{-1} l_0^ν. So h is the σ_∞-twisted conjugate of η^{-1} by c.

Step 2. To express h as a twisted conjugate of η itself, Grothendieck uses the cocycle identity η^{-1} = σ_∞(η). From it he writes η^{-1} = η^{-1}·η·σ_∞(η^{-1})^{-1}. This gives (28bis): h = (cη^{-1})·η·σ_∞(cη^{-1})^{-1}.

Step 3 (case h = 1). Formula (27) gives g = (l_0^ν f)^{-1} ξ ρ(l_0^ν f). Hence solutions of the 'trivialisation' (non-abelian coboundary) equations (29), g = αρ(α)^{-1} and ξ = α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1}, correspond via (30): α = f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0.

Step 4 (case g = 1). Similarly, solutions of (31), h = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} and η = β_0σ_∞(β_0)^{-1}, correspond via (32): β = (f^{-1} l_0^ν η^{-1}) β_0.

Step 5. Grothendieck comments on the asymmetry: (32) carries an extra factor η^{-1}, which is expressible through β_0. He attributes this to the choice in (6) of defining l_0 from the element σ_∞ρ = ε_0 (apparently as its square in the extended group) rather than from ρσ_∞ = ε_1.

Purpose. The aim is bookkeeping for the non-abelian H^1 of the cyclic groups ⟨ρ⟩ and ⟨σ_∞⟩ acting on \hat\Pi_{0,3}. It relates trivialisations of the defects g, h to trivialisations of the normalised cocycles ξ, η. This prepares the next page, where everything is pushed into the quotient GL(2,\hat Z)/±1.
errors: No genuine error; (28bis), (30) and (32) check out by direct substitution, given η·σ_∞(η) = 1, which follows from η = β_0σ_∞(β_0)^{-1}.

The asymmetry noted in (32) is partly cosmetic: since η^{-1} = σ_∞(β_0)β_0^{-1}, one has η^{-1}β_0 = σ_∞(β_0). So (32) simplifies to β = f^{-1} l_0^ν σ_∞(β_0), formally parallel to (30) (with a σ_∞-twist on β_0 instead of an extra factor). Grothendieck seems to half-say this ('par les coefficients de β_0') but does not write the simplified form.
The struck-through first attempt η^{-1} = η^{-1}·η·σ_∞(η^{-1}) is wrong by an inverse; he corrected it.

ideas.what: Expressing the defect elements g, h of the 2- and 3-cycle-type relations as ρ- resp. σ_∞-twisted conjugates of normalised cocycles ξ, η by f^{-1} l_0^{±ν}
ideas.modern_name: twisted conjugation / non-abelian cohomology H^1(Z/2), H^1(Z/3) with coefficients in the free profinite group; GT relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for the GT relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the S_3/GL(2) picture; these computations are unpublished (La Longue Marche manuscripts)

ideas.what: Correspondence between solutions of coboundary equations g = αρ(α)^{-1} and ξ = α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1} (and the σ_∞ analogue)
ideas.modern_name: change of base point in twisted-conjugacy classes; triviality of non-abelian H^1 classes

deep.surprise_reason: Routine algebraic bookkeeping of twisted cocycles inside a longer unpublished computation on GT-type relations. It is correct and context-dependent, but contains no new result or connection beyond what the GT literature already covers.
transcription_corrections: Every 'y' in the transcription is Grothendieck's η. Line 4 should read η^{-1} = σ_∞(η) = η^{-1}·η·σ_∞(η^{-1})^{-1}, and (28bis) is h = (f^{-1}l_0^ν η^{-1}) η σ_∞(f^{-1}l_0^ν η^{-1})^{-1}.

In 'La dissymétrie entre ces deux formules (32) étant un peu plus compliquée que (30)', a phrase is missing; probably 'La dissymétrie entre ces deux formules ((32) étant un peu plus compliquée que (30), par le facteur supplémentaire η^{-1} (s'exprimant par les coefficients de β_0)) provient du fait que...'.
'formule de Cech (6)' is doubtful; likely just 'la formule (6), première forme'.
The last line likely reads 'où l_0 est défini comme le carré de σ_∞ρ = ε_0, et non de ρσ_∞ = ε_1' ('f' is a misreading of ρ, 'conj' of 'carré').
